Important.title: Value-equality predicates do not enforce the advertised bitwise state, repeated-forward and cache/readback identity
Important.problem: torch.equal treats signed zeros as equal and can accept equal values across dtypes. np.array_equal also accepts+0/-0. The reference forward dtype/shape is not independently required at line37. These predicates therefore allow different FP32 byte strings or a non-FP32 reference while returning repeated_forward_FP32_bitwise_equal:true and accepting cache readback.
reproduced_cases: Fresh encoder calls output+0 and-0 at one FP32 scalar. Bytes00000000 versus00000080 differ, but the worker returns repeated_forward_FP32_bitwise_equal:true.
Second forward returns FP64 values exactly equal to first FP32 values; no ValueError is raised.

First legitimate source-only run writes a real temporary cache with negative zero. A later complete fresh forward produces positive zero and matches itself; write_role reuses the existing complete cache and np.array_equal accepts old negative-zero cache versus fresh positive-zero despite different raw bytes.

Important.recommendation: Use strict dtype/shape plus contiguous raw-byte equality for Torch state/forward tensors and NumPy feature/head arrays. Independently require both fresh outputs to be finite FP32 with the exact expected shape. Observe signed-zero,second-dtype and existing-cache bit mismatch regressions failing before the fix and passing afterwards.
